picks.title: Apple's updated App Store rules go after 'nudify' AI apps
picks.excerpt: Apple's revised App Store Review Guidelines require developers to prevent and remove sexualized deepfakes, targeting AI 'nudify' apps.
picks.rationale: A new platform rule, published as revised App Store Review Guidelines, puts concrete obligations on any developer shipping generative-image features. It is a different event from the 10-03 EU nudify ban and the 10-05 Minnesota ruling. Copy should cite the guideline text, which is the primary document. Check this does not clash with a gadgets pick.

picks.title: North Korea says it tested new AI-powered torpedo system
picks.excerpt: KCNA says North Korea tested the Zam-2.0 torpedo, which uses artificial intelligence to aid target detection and guidance, days after underwater-launched cruise missile tests. (time from page display 09:52 GMT+2)
picks.rationale: A new state announcement of an AI-guided weapons test, on the geopolitics axis. The AI capability is entirely North Korea's claim, so attribute it to KCNA and do not present it as verified.

picks.title: The Case for DUV Controls
picks.excerpt: Former NSC tech official Saif Khan makes the case for extending export controls to DUV lithography tools to constrain China's AI chip production.
picks.rationale: A former NSC official proposes extending chip export controls to DUV lithography, which would affect AI compute supply. It is not commentary on a story we already published. Present it as Khan's argued proposal and attribute it to him, not as a government decision.

picks.title: What the West can learn from AI optimists in the rest of the world
picks.excerpt: Public opinion on AI diverges sharply: enthusiastic, necessity-driven adoption in the developing world contrasts with an anxiety-ridden West.
picks.rationale: Replacement pick. It covers the public-opinion axis, which had no other pick today: Rest of World compares how attitudes to AI differ between the developing world and the West. This is analysis, not a decision, so the copy should present it as Rest of World's reading of survey and field evidence, attribute it, and stay neutral. It does not repeat the 10-13 US 'chatbot refuseniks' survey card or the 10-17 Rest of World open-weight models card.
